description: Typical inland and coastal Northeast hatch calendar for trout and warmwater tying prep.

1.notes: Slow winter water — tiny midges and dark stonefly nymphs. Streamers for deeper pools on mild days.

2.notes: Continue midge focus; black stones start on freestones during thaws. Soft hackles in slow seams.

3.notes: First reliable BWO windows on overcast afternoons. Stock baetis dries, emergers, and pheasant tails.

4.notes: Classic early mayfly season. Hendrickson and Quill Gordon dries/emergers; tan caddis begin late month.

5.notes: Peak spring diversity. Elk-hair caddis, march brown patterns, and streamers for high water.

6.notes: Sulphur evenings and cahill afternoons. Start terrestrial boxes; green drake where local.

7.notes: Trico spinner falls at dawn; terrestrials midday. Iso nymphs and dries on freestones.

8.notes: Terrestrial peak — hoppers and ants. Warmwater poppers/streamers for bass ponds and rivers.

9.notes: Fall BWO return; ants after rains. Streamers as baitfish move — excellent for larger trout.

10.notes: Cooling water — olives and large autumn caddis. Stock streamers for pre-spawn aggression.

11.notes: Sparse surface action; focus nymphs and streamers. Midge clusters on calm late-season days.

12.notes: Bench season — rebuild midge and nymph boxes, restock streamers for winter trips.
